title: Pest management intervention strategic and logistical planning processes

lessons.title: Planning interventions at work
lessons.html:
From classroom plan to workplace plan

In this module you take part in planning real interventions with your mentor, and progressively prepare plans yourself for approval. Real planning involves trade-offs: client budgets, production schedules, harvest pressure, weather, stock availability and staff rosters.

Typical planning tasks

  • Drafting objectives and selecting methods from inspection findings.
  • Checking product labels and registration for each target pest and site.
  • Calculating areas, volumes, tonnages and product quantities.
  • Writing job-specific risk assessments.
  • Preparing quotations and proposals.
  • Scheduling teams, vehicles and equipment.
  • Ordering stock and checking PPE and calibration.
  • Drafting notices for occupants and neighbours.

Scenario: planning a harvest-season programme

A grain cooperative asks for a pest plan before harvest. With your mentor you plan: cleaning and structural treatment of empty bins and pits in the weeks before intake; rodent bait station layout around the complex; monthly grain sampling during storage; and fumigation contingency for bins that exceed the agreed insect threshold. Logistics include confirming registered products and stock, booking a registered fumigator for possible bin fumigations, checking sealing materials and gas monitors, and agreeing with the silo manager when bins can be isolated. The plan states which tasks belong to the cooperative, such as cleaning spillage and repairing aeration seals.

Checking your work

Have every calculation and plan checked by your mentor before it reaches the client. Treat corrections as learning, and note them in your logbook.

lessons.title: Managing logistics and recording your learning
lessons.html:
Logistics in practice

Good plans fail when logistics fail: a fumigator arrives without monitors, the knapsacks were not calibrated, or the product is out of stock in peak season. Practise these logistics checks before every job.

AreaCheck before the job
PeopleCorrect registrations, numbers, standby person, supervisor
ProductsRegistered for the use, quantity, batch, in date, SDS available
EquipmentCalibrated, serviced, spare parts, gas monitors charged
PPESizes, cartridges and canisters in date, fit test current
VehicleSecure chemical compartment, spill kit, fire extinguisher
ClientWritten approval, access arranged, preparation instructions sent

Adapting the plan

Plans change. Rain may postpone herbicide work; a client may not complete preparation; a bin may not seal. Practise deciding, with your mentor, whether to proceed, adapt or postpone, and record the reasons. Never adapt a plan in a way that breaks the label or safety requirements.

Portfolio evidence

  • Plans and risk assessments you drafted, with mentor comments.
  • Calculation sheets.
  • Quotations and schedules.
  • Logistics checklists completed before jobs.
  • Reflections on plans that worked and plans that needed changing.

Key points

  • Workplace planning balances pest needs with client operations, budget and resources.
  • Check labels, calculations and risk assessments, and have them verified by your mentor.
  • State client responsibilities clearly in every plan.
  • Complete logistics checks on people, products, equipment, PPE, vehicle and client before each job.
  • Adapt plans safely within the label and record the reasons.
